name: Pixel icon
region: Xerox PARC and Apple, United States
summary: Icons drawn on a hard pixel grid, one square at a time. Each pixel is on or off, edges are stairs, and the set has 1 to 16 colours. The style began with low screen resolution and returns now as a retro choice.

philosophy.core_thesis: An icon is a set of square pixels on a fixed grid, and the grid is part of the look, not a limit to hide.
design_principles: Draw on a grid of 16 × 16 or 32 × 32 px, and place every edge on a whole pixel.
Use straight runs and 1:1, 1:2 or 2:1 steps for diagonals; a curve is a sequence of these steps.
Keep the outline 1 px wide at 16 px and 2 px wide at 32 px.
Use 1 to 4 colours for a UI glyph and at most 16 for an app icon, with no anti-alias.
Scale only by whole multiples (2×, 3×, 4×) with nearest-neighbour sampling.
Leave a 1 px clear margin inside the grid on each side.
anti_patterns: Smooth vector curves on a pixel grid
Scale by a fraction such as 1.5×

grid.keylines: One square keyline of 22 × 22 px; no circle keyline, because a circle becomes a stair shape.

stroke.rule: No vector stroke. A line is a run of whole pixels, 1 px wide at 16 px and 2 px wide at 32 px.

shape.primitives: Squares, straight runs and stair steps of 1:1, 1:2 or 2:1 px; no curve except a stair curve.
shape.optical_size: Redraw each size by hand: a 16 px icon has fewer parts than a 32 px icon, never a scaled copy.

colour.strategy: One ink colour for a UI glyph; 4 to 16 flat colours for an app icon, from a fixed system palette.

perspective_and_light.light: No light model; one shade step of 1 px may mark a lower or right edge.
perspective_and_light.shadow: None, or a 1 px offset shadow in one darker colour.

metaphor.typical: A disk, a folder, a trash can, a document, a clock and a hand cursor.
metaphor.treatment: Literal office objects reduced to their silhouette at 16 or 32 px.

evidence.title: Pixel Icon Library: home
evidence.credit: HackerNoon Pixel Icon Library at commit 5fe05c9; icon files under CC BY 4.0

emotion.target_response: Warm recognition of early computers: the icons feel exact, small and a little playful.

use_cases: developer tools with a playful voice
avoid_when: The product needs a calm, premium or medical tone.
The icon must scale to any fraction of its size.

modifiers.how: Keep the silhouette and the 24 px grid; trace it as a 2 px vector stroke with round caps and a 2 px corner radius.
Keep the hard pixel look; rotate the object to an isometric view with 2:1 pixel diagonals.

stroke_width.note: A line is a run of whole pixels, not a vector stroke.

corner_radius.note: A corner is a stair of whole pixels, never a curve.

sources.title: Susan Kare, icon work for the Apple Macintosh (1984), as described in the Wikipedia article
